items.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023
items.q: we had a similar thing in the new James Bond film that I wrote some brass arrangements for because there’s a whole scene in Cuba where there’s a big fight. But what they wanted to do was get the sort of salsa/Cuban element into the James Bond/Hans Zimmer milieu.

ctx.x: You were — there’s some marvelous interviews online that I have watched and I think you were describing a scene from a James Bond movie. And you used the word absurd. So I started thinking about adjectives and what goes through your head after you watch a sequence, even before you go to the piano or have a pencil in hand that might musicalize an adjective like absurd?

Well I mean taking for example that particular sequence, which I know is the GoldenEye tank chase. I had arranged and conducted the whole score for another composer. And when they did the — came to dub the film, they basically weren’t happy with what he’d written and they contacted me and said would you write something for this. And I said well I know what you want but I won’t do it unless the composer is happy, because I’m his arranger. And they phoned him and he — I think grudgingly — said yeah, I’m not going…
That was going through my head there. How much do you have to be aware of what’s been written so far by another composer and try not to sound like an obvious change of arranger/composer.
